title: Dedicated capacity steadywave + spike fidelity benchmark
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Create a reproducible benchmark harness that validates Dedicated capacity behavior across mixed-mode traffic: 'steadywave' (long-lived ~tokens/sec with small jitter) and 'spike' (short high-throughput bursts). Goals: measure sustained tokens/sec, p95 latency contours, token-level error amplification during autoscale transitions, and detect regressions vs historical baselines. Deliverables: (1) YAML-driven scenario definitions for the load generator, (2) standardized metrics dashboard and alert thresholds, (3) regression test runner with automated baseline comparison and PR gating, (4) recommendations for autoscaler setpoints and cooldown tuning.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Khatri: Initial write-up and scope. Priority set because customers have reported latency regressions during mixed workloads on Dedicated pools. Proposed to reuse parts of the existing soak harness but with a different traffic profile generator (steadywave + intermittent spikes).

2026-02-18 - Marco Liao: Spike profile prototype implemented in loadgen v0.9. Added 'prefix hot' option to model KV-cache warming so we can measure cache-miss amplification during spikes. Found early that token/sec plateaus at lower rate than expected on a 4xA100 pool when sequence length > 1024.

2026-02-22 - QA: Ran first 6-hour steadywave run against dedicated-staging. Observed p95 latency drift from 220ms -> 380ms as available slots saturated; tail correlated with increased GC cycles on host process. Attached chart: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/bench/steadywave-2026-02-22

2026-02-25 - Marco Liao: Added regression comparator script. It computes delta_p95 and pct_tokens_delta against a stored baseline and emits a failing CI marker when p95 increases by >15% while tokens/sec drops by >10% for 10-minute windows. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9187
2026-02-27 - Infra: Noted that autoscaler scale-up latency (API provisioning) added ~30s median during a controlled 2x spike. Filed ENG-140300 to follow up on autoscaler API throttling.
progress_updates: Prototype load profiles (steadywave + spike) implemented and validated on staging clusters.
Baseline run completed and stored; comparator script produces human-readable summary and machine exit codes for CI.
Found a reproducible regression pattern tied to large-sequence (>1024) requests overlapping with autoscaler transitions.
Draft recommended autoscaler setpoints: warm-burst threshold = 60% utilization, hard-burst threshold = 85%, cooldown = 45s. These are preliminary and require validation against 8-hour soak runs.
test_plan: 1) Define steadywave: sustained 60-70% target utilization with jitter +/-7% across 6 hours. 2) Insert spikes: 30s full-burst (2.5-3x steady tokens/sec) every 12 minutes for the first 3 hours, then randomized spikes for the next 3 hours. 3) Measure: tokens/sec (1m and 1s windows), p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, KV cache hit ratio, autoscaler events and scale latency. 4) Run comparator: fail if p95 increases >15% vs baseline or tokens/sec drops >10% persistently for 10 minutes. 5) Create run artifacts: load profiles, Grafana dashboard snapshot, and a containment checklist for incidents.
open_risks: Autoscaler API provisioning time skews results for short spikes — may require synthetic acceleration or an infra change (follow-up ENG-140300).
Host-level GC and driver memory pressure observed during long steadywave runs; may require kernel-level tuning or runtime memory cap adjustments.
KV-cache warmup is sensitive to prompt prefix diversity; if customer workloads have high prefix entropy, steadywave numbers will not reflect real-world cold-start behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can run end-to-end in CI and produce a clear pass/fail via comparator script. 2) Produce reproducible baseline with <5% run-to-run variance for tokens/sec over 6-hour steadywave. 3) Documented autoscaler tuning recommendations with supporting runs (at least 2 independent confirmations). 4) PR merged for harness and dashboards with owner approvals from infra and reliability.
next_steps: Validate recommended setpoints with 12-hour overnight run on canary Dedicated pool.
Collaborate with Infra to reduce autoscaler API latency or add a synthetic fast-path for short spikes.
Add a 'customer-like' workload generator mode that injects prefix entropy to measure worst-case token/sec impact.
